title: Evaluation of "ACT for Health", an Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)-based mental health promotion program for stressed students - a pilot study
summary: Students suffer a deterioration in their health over the course of their studies compared to the general population, with events such as the COVID-19 pandemic also contributing to this. Therefore, it is important to develop prevention and support programs for students to promote mental health. In this study, such a program, based on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), will be tested for the first time in terms of its effectiveness for students reporting higher levels of psychological distress, following an initial successful trial for psychotherapy students with low psychological distress. ACT is a modern method of behavioral therapy that supports people in dealing with difficulties in their lives in a psychologically flexible way (promotion of so-called psychological flexibility). Previous studies have shown that people who have psychological flexibility experience less stress, feel better, can cope with problems more easily and have a higher quality of life and performance. Students who contact the psychological counseling service of the Studentenwerk Schleswig-Holstein due to their stress are offered the "ACT for Health" training with 6 training sessions of 90 minutes each at weekly intervals.  The data collection takes place before the start of the training, three weeks after the start of the training, one week after the end of the training and four and 12 weeks after the end of the training. The main focus is on changes in psychological flexibility at the end of the training, as well as changes in psychological stress, the ability to deal with emotions, quality of life, psychological resilience and self-compassion. Interviews will be used to record the stress experienced by students in everyday life and their experiences with the "ACT for Health" program.

interventions.name: Psychologically distressed students who receive training in 6 units using Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) to promote psychological flexibility

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Students with sufficient knowledge of the German language who present themselves at the counseling centers of the Studentenwerk SH due to mental stress, who could benefit from "ACT for Health" from the counselors' point of view and who are interested in participating in the "ACT for Health" training
Exclusion criteria:
Students who are foreseeably unable to participate regularly and fully in the training offered and/or acute suicidal tendencies and mental illnesses of a degree of severity for which prompt, disorder-specific therapy in an inpatient setting is indicated
